method: Original summaries verified against publisher, author, Folger and exact-edition catalogue evidence. ISBN, title, author and language guard every text. The omnibus and short-story collection are explicitly identified. No generic withdrawn-provider fallback is enabled.

entries.title: The Secret Adversary
entries.author: Agatha Christie
entries.text: Tommy and Tuppence need work, money and a little excitement. Their answer is to start Young Adventurers Ltd., offering their services for whatever unusual assignment comes along. A job from Mr Whittington quickly turns their optimistic business venture into something far more dangerous. The search for a secret and the identity of a powerful adversary drive this adventure, which introduces Christie's recurring detective partnership. First published in 1922, it is her second novel and the beginning of Tommy and Tuppence's investigations.
entries.identityNotes: Exact Ancient Wisdom Publications edition ISBN verified through OL27790720M; official author estate supplies the work synopsis.

entries.title: Midsummer Night's Dream
entries.author: William Shakespeare
entries.text: A wedding in Athens brings together several very different kinds of love. Outside the city, four young lovers become entangled in shifting affections, while the fairy rulers Oberon and Titania quarrel over a child. Magic adds to the confusion when Bottom, a weaver rehearsing a play with his companions, acquires a donkey's head and becomes the object of Titania's desire. Shakespeare's comedy moves between the human and fairy worlds, bringing romance, transformation and an amateur theatrical performance into the same midsummer adventure.
entries.identityNotes: AD Classic edition ISBN verified through OL57786764M. Folger supplies play-level evidence; the selected edition is not represented as a Folger edition.

entries.title: The Mystery of the Blue Train
entries.author: Agatha Christie
entries.text: A journey towards the Riviera becomes a murder investigation when Ruth Kettering, the daughter of a millionaire, is killed aboard the Blue Train. Her valuable jewels are missing, leaving Hercule Poirot to investigate a crime behind the luxury of the railway setting. The combination of a murdered heiress and stolen valuables makes this a case about appearances as well as evidence. Published in 1928, the novel expands on Christie's earlier Poirot short story The Plymouth Express.
entries.identityNotes: Bantam edition ISBN verified through OL7826093M. This is the Blue Train novel, not Murder on the Orient Express.

entries.title: Antony and Cleopatra
entries.author: William Shakespeare
entries.text: Mark Antony shares power in Rome with Octavius Caesar and Lepidus, but his relationship with Egypt's Queen Cleopatra pulls him towards a competing allegiance. Political cooperation gives way to rivalry as Caesar strengthens his position and Antony struggles to reconcile love with military duty. Shakespeare's tragedy places the lovers' volatile intimacy alongside the contest for control of the Roman world. Marriage, suspicion and shifting alliances connect private choices to public consequences, making the struggle between Antony and Caesar inseparable from Cleopatra's fate.
entries.identityNotes: Arden Third Series hardback ISBN verified through OL8770899M. Folger is evidence for the play, not the edition imprint. First printing 1623 verified separately; catalogue work year 1734 requires correction.

entries.title: Three Fates
entries.author: Nora Roberts
entries.text: A silver statue carried away from the sinking Lusitania becomes a treasured family possession, until another theft sends three Irish siblings in search of it. Malachi, Gideon and Rebecca Sullivan want to recover their inheritance and reunite it with the other two figures known as the Three Fates. Their pursuit crosses Europe and reaches New York, drawing a scholar and a determined rival into the hunt. Nora Roberts combines the search for a scattered treasure with romance, family loyalty and competing ambitions.
entries.identityNotes: G.P. Putnam edition ISBN verified through OL32725364M; publisher page identifies the same work in a later edition. No edition date or format is borrowed from that page.

entries.title: Face The Fire
entries.author: Nora Roberts
entries.text: Mia Devlin has built an independent life after Sam Logan left Three Sisters Island and broke her heart. When he returns as the owner of the island's hotel, he hopes to renew their relationship, but Mia's hurt makes reconciliation difficult. Their attraction remains, and an approaching supernatural challenge means that his powers may matter as much as his feelings. This final novel in Nora Roberts's Three Sisters Island trilogy brings Mia's romance and the series' magical concerns together in its concluding story.
entries.identityNotes: Exact Jove large-print hardcover ISBN verified through OL7916046M. PRH page supports work content and trilogy position, not the selected edition format.

entries.title: The Villa
entries.author: Nora Roberts
entries.text: Sophia Giambelli understands the marketing side of her family's wine business. A merger with the MacMillan winery forces her to work closely with Tyler MacMillan, whose expertise lies in growing the grapes. As they exchange skills, professional rivalry develops alongside an attraction neither can easily set aside. The future of the combined company is already uncertain when sabotage puts the family and its livelihood at risk. Set in Napa Valley, Nora Roberts's romantic suspense novel connects a business alliance with personal loyalties and danger.
entries.identityNotes: Berkley Trade edition ISBN verified through OL10216562M. Publisher synopsis matches the work; dates and ISBNs of other editions are not substituted.

entries.title: The mysterious Mr Quin
entries.author: Agatha Christie
entries.text: Mr Satterthwaite is accustomed to watching other people's lives, but a mysterious arrival at a New Year's Eve gathering draws him into a different kind of drama. Harley Quin appears at moments when an unresolved mystery needs a fresh perspective, then vanishes as unexpectedly as he came. Across twelve stories, the two men uncover separate puzzles through observation and encounters that carry an uncanny atmosphere. This 1930 collection follows their unusual partnership, with Quin's elusive presence connecting otherwise distinct investigations.
entries.identityNotes: Exact HarperCollins edition ISBN verified through OL30114438M, including original 1930 publication note. Official estate identifies twelve-story collection. Its canonical source slug intentionally spells myserious.

entries.title: Time and Again
entries.author: Nora Roberts
entries.text: Time and Again brings together Time Was and Times Change, two connected romances about the Hornblower brothers. In the first, Caleb arrives from the twenty-third century and finds himself drawn to Liberty Stone while trying to return home. In the second, Jacob travels back to retrieve his brother, only to meet Liberty's sister Sunny and question his own certainty about love. The collection follows both relationships, using time travel to put the brothers' plans for the future in conflict with the lives they discover in the past.
entries.identityNotes: Exact Thorndike large-print edition ISBN verified through OL32740473M and Google Books catalogue (Hornblower Brothers books 1–2). Macmillan independently confirms both titles and plots. This is an omnibus, not a standalone third novel.

entries.title: Reluctant Mistress, Blackmailed Wife
entries.author: Lynne Graham
entries.text: Katie is raising twin boys and would prefer to keep their father out of her life. Financial hardship leads her to seek help from Alexandros Christakis, a wealthy Greek businessman, but his response comes with a demand for marriage. Their renewed contact exposes the attraction that remains between them without resolving the differences between them. Lynne Graham's romance centres on the pressure surrounding Katie's decision, the needs of her children and a relationship shaped by unequal resources and unresolved feelings.
entries.identityNotes: Exact Harlequin Mills & Boon edition ISBN verified through OL28988064M. Author page confirms Katie, twin sons, Alexandros Christakis and the marriage demand.
